result.title: Look Back, Correct Forward: Error Feedback Calibration for Time Series Forecasting
result.summary: Time series forecasting models are increasingly deployed in continuously evolving environments. After a forecast is issued, future observations gradually arrive and reveal how the model has failed. Existing methods mainly treat such observations as supervision for parameter updates. However, it remains unclear whether verified forecasting errors can themselves provide causal feedback for correcting future predictions. To address this, we introduce Error Feedback Calibration (EFC), a fully test-time framework for deterministic post-hoc correction of time series forecasting. EFC constructs a Causal Error Diagonal (CED) from revealed errors of overlapping historical forecasts, providing a fresh view of the frozen forecaster's recent failure behavior. Then Cumulative Error Transport (CET) maps this error state to future residuals using cumulative estimation, while temporal out-of-sample validation controls the correction strength. Temporal Residual Learning (TRL) further predicts only the residual structure left after CET from recent CED trajectories, rather than relearning the entire forecasting error. Extensive experiments across forecasting backbones and datasets show that EFC broadly improves forecasting performance while substantially controlling harmful over correction.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Error Feedback Calibration（EFC）这一完全测试时、无需训练的事后校正框架：用重叠历史预报已揭示的误差构造 Causal Error Diagonal，经 Cumulative Error Transport 累积估计映射为未来残差，由时序样本外验证控制校正强度，并用 Temporal Residual Learning 只预测 CET 后剩余的残差结构；在多种预测骨干与数据集上提升精度并抑制过度校正。
